findings.claim: The core scenario is rejected. The data-type guard includes `|| type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. Any `T` loaded from a compiled referenced assembly (a real metadata reference such as Project A's DLL) has no declaring syntax references. So `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>` reports MsgPack021 ('only accessible, non-generic, non-abstract classes and structs are supported') and emits no formatter body. The user's class then fails with CS0535. Only `T` declared in source in the same compilation (or reached through an in-memory CompilationReference) works, which contradicts the acceptance criterion 'even when T is declared in a referenced assembly'.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterMetadataTypeTests.FormatterForTypeFromCompiledReferencedAssembly_IsGenerated. It emits ProjectA to a PE image, references it via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage, and runs MessagePackGenerator. On head the generator reports MsgPack021 and the output compilation has CS0535 errors.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on `T` are never honoured. When no surrogate is given, `CreateContractlessMembers` always serializes every public read-write member by name. It ignores `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` int keys and `[IgnoreMember]` (and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]`/`[IgnoreDataMember]`) declared on `T`. Example: `T` has `[MessagePackObject] class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int B {get;set;} }`. The generated formatter writes a string-keyed map containing both A and B, instead of an int-keyed array containing only A. This violates the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.'

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect lines 88-96: the `surrogate is null` branch calls CreateContractlessMembers(type), which uses only IsPublicReadWrite and never inspects referenceSymbols.KeyAttribute or IgnoreAttribute on `type`'s members. Confirm with a generator run where T carries [Key]/[IgnoreMember] and inspect the generated formatter for an ignored member name and string keys.
